messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: p99 latency spike observed for eu-west streaming ingress and multiple TLS handshake failures — paging dave-oncall. Metric: streaming_tail_p99 eu-west = 2.1s (baseline 120ms), handshake_fail_rate = 6.7% (baseline 0.4%).

maya.singh: seeing the page, joining. any client-visible errors?

raj.patel: yes, we have increased 503s on the streaming proxy (~8% errors per 1m) and a big jump in streaming stalls counts in the trace logs.

carla.neteng: quick summary from net metrics: inter-AZ path between azb and azc shows packet loss spikes and SYN retransmits. NAT ephemeral port exhaustion signs in the eu-west NAT fleet (conntrack entries ~95% used). Also DNS timeouts from a subset of hosts in azc.

maya.singh: that combo would explain handshake retries and long stalls. can someone confirm which services are impacted?

raj.patel: primarily streaming-proxy (ingress), some generate endpoints hitting dedicated model racks; non-stream generation mostly OK. customer-impact: live streaming sessions show intermittent stalls and reconnects. seeing more impact on long-lived connections.


dave-oncall: I'm going to page neteng and try quick mitigations. carla?

carla.neteng: on it. starting rolling restart of the NAT gateway daemon on eu-west-nat-2 to free ephemeral ports. also enabling short-term ephemeral port range expansion on the NAT host pool.

opsbot: Command run: ssh nat-2-eu-west && sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='32768 60999' — SUCCESS

maya.singh: good. I'll also trigger a probe reroute for streaming-proxy to avoid azc for new connections: updating route policy to prefer azb->azb local path.

raj.patel: applying canary: updating k8s service annotation to prefer endpointSubset in azb for streaming-proxy.

maya.singh: applied. new sessions should avoid the flaky path within 30s.

incident-bot: alert: p95 back down to 540ms from 1.2s; p99 still elevated at 1.9s. 503s reduced to ~5%.

carla.neteng: conntrack shoehorn reduced after port range change, but we still see elevated SYN retransmits on azc egress router. routing flaps traced to a flakey interface on switch 13 in azc. I’ve opened a ticket with cloud provider and initiated fabric-level failover for that rack.

dave-oncall: what's the impact on customer SLAs? pm-elena, can you advise on external comms?

pm-elena: collecting affected customer list now. initial glance: 3 enterprise customers in eu-west with active live sessions, one partner integration experiencing reconnects. Will draft a short status note: "Temporary streaming degradations in eu-west; mitigation in progress."

raj.patel: next: looking at streaming stall traces — many show TLS handshake stalled at initial ClientHello -> SYN-ACK not completing, then retries. Also a subset shows DNS lookup latency spikes (200ms -> 2s).

maya.singh: let's apply two-pronged mitigations: 1) force new connections to fallback DNS resolver pool (eu-dns-hot) via resolver config on proxy; 2) restart streaming-proxy instances with cleared TCP stacks to drop half-open states: kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy -n prod --namespace=prod (canary first).

opsbot: Command run: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment streaming-proxy --selector=canary=false — started canary restart 3/30 pods.

carla.neteng: fabric failover completed for the affected rack; cloud provider reports the interface as flapping and removed it from rotation. Expect less packet loss in 2 mins.

incident-bot: metric update: streaming_tail_p95 eu-west = 230ms, p99 = 820ms. handshake_fail_rate down to 1.2%. 503s at 1.5%.

dave-oncall: looks improved but not fully healed. keep monitoring for 30m. if p99 > 1s after that we escalate to war room.

maya.singh: agree. setting a dashboard alert for p99 > 1s for 15m.

raj.patel: logs show a lingering population of half-open sessions on some proxies. I recommend we rotate the remaining proxies during a controlled window to flush TCP state. will coordinate with deploy window.

carla.neteng: cloud provider also recommended NAT pool sharding to reduce collision and ephemeral exhaustion risk. I’ll create a follow-up ticket to expand the NAT pool and add automated port usage alerting.

pm-elena: drafting notice: "We observed transient streaming degradation in eu-west causing reconnects and stalls for some live sessions. We mitigated via routing failover, NAT host configuration changes, and restarting affected proxies. Monitoring continues and we will follow up with a post-incident summary." Any technical details to add?

maya.singh: add that we saw inter-AZ route flaps and ephemeral port pressure causing elevated TLS handshake retries and packet loss, and that we've implemented temporary port-range expansion and rack-level fabric failover.

dave-oncall: I'll take a full incident write-up after we’ve been stable for 1h. for now: set status to "degraded — mitigations applied" and mark P0? I'd call it P1 due to partial customer impact.

incident-bot: incident status changed by dave-oncall: DEGRADED -> MITIGATION APPLIED (P1).

opsbot: Runbook note: recommended commands used during triage:
```
# check conntrack usage
sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
# expand port range
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='32768 60999'
# restart streaming proxies (canary)
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment streaming-proxy --selector=canary=false
# force resolver switch
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/streaming-proxy DNS_RESOLVER_POOL=eu-dns-hot
```

maya.singh: thanks everyone. I'll stay watching the dashboards. tagging follow-ups: @carla.neteng to own NAT sharding ticket, @raj.patel to own proxy rotate plan, @pm-elena to finalize customer comms.

carla.neteng: ack. will create ticket and include provider contact + timeline.

raj.patel: will schedule proxy rotation during low traffic window in 45m.

pm-elena: posting status update to customers now.

incident-bot: final metric snapshot at last_message_ts: p95=210ms, p99=480ms, handshake_fail_rate=0.5%, streaming_503s=0.8%. Monitoring ongoing.

maya.singh: marking this thread as handed off to follow-ups. will reopen if backend SLOs breach again. :white_check_mark:
